programme.title: Worth the Hype

programme.desc: Grab your fork and join Frankie Celenza as he eats his way through New Jersey's most iconic spots that are worth the hype. From silky custard cups to pasta Picasso to giant pizza slices, just add PEPSI and you've got the perfect pairing.

programme.title: Worth the Hype
programme.sub-title: Smothered Pork Chops, Ramen & Fried Flounder in Charleston
programme.desc: Pull up a seat and join Frankie Celenza as he eats his way through Charleston, South Carolina's most iconic spots that are worth the hype. From coastal soul to Lowcountry classics, just add PEPSI and you've got the perfect pairing.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.desc: Luke arrives in Saigon for a breakfast of iced coffee with condensed milk and a vermicelli noodle dish. Later, he visits his favorite Pho restaurant, then cooks up some spicy Chili Crab Claws.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.desc: Luke continues his street food journey in Bangkok where he searches for the best Tom Yum soup and entertains the locals with a rare Thai delicacy.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.sub-title: Malaysian Flying Noodles and Pork Bone Soup
programme.desc: In Kuala Lumpur, Luke meets the famous Mr Hung with a reputation for flying instant noodles and Mr Sou who cooks a hearty Pork Bone Soup with medicinal herbal properties.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.desc: Luke continues his street food adventure exploring Jakarta, a melting pot of diverse cultural cuisines, where he indulges in an Indonesian dessert, the sweet Martabak, known as the "King of Street Food".

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: Andalusia, now crossed by high-speed and modernized rail lines, unveils its rich culture and landscapes; along the journey, we visit cities like Seville, Granada with its famed Alhambra and Guadix near the Tabernas Desert.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: Corsica, the Island of Beauty, is best explored by railway; from Mediterranean waters to towering peaks, stops include Algajola for a seaside dive, Vizzavona on the GR20 trail and historic cities like Corte with its citadel.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: The Little Yellow Train winds through the Eastern Pyrenees, crossing the Cerdan plateau, the historic Gisclard railway suspension bridge and the Grandes Canalettes caves, known as the underground Versailles of the Pyrenees.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: In Greece, the Intercity Express travels from Thessaloniki to Athens, passing sites like the Meteora peaks, Delphi ruins and the Acropolis; the journey continues to the Peloponnese on Greece's last cogwheel train.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: In Portugal, in the Douro River Valley, a steam locomotive and a small historic train will take you in turn to the water's edge, on the only railroad line in the world that crosses three World Heritage Sites classified by UNESCO.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: The Cinque Terre Express runs along Italy's northern coast east of Genoa; passing through five UNESCO-listed villages, it offers coastal views and access to cobbled streets, harbors, terraced vineyards and pastel-colored houses.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie is taking spaghetti bolognese to the next level and re-creating a mind-blowing Jewish-Italian recipe. There's also beef stew with pappardelle.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie visits the pizza capital of Italy to learn recipes from the locals and tries acquapazza, fish poached in crazy water.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie gets a masterclass in Sicilian sweets and cooking up an epic tuna, prawn and pistachio spaghetti. There's also some chocolaty cannoli.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.desc: Considering the nature and scope of biblical archeology; how the Book of Genesis makes its case for the existence of a single God; archeological evidence for a great flood in ancient times; its possible connection to the biblical story of Noah.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.desc: The symbolism of the tower and pyramid in ancient architecture; the Egyptian step pyramid at Saqqara; the Mesopotamian ziggurat's role in religious life and ritual; parallels between the building of ziggurats and the story of the Tower of Babel.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.desc: Tracing the life of Abraham from his origins; how Abraham follows the call of God in traveling to Canaan; historical evidence related to the events of Abraham's journey; the narrative of Abraham's search for an heir to his clan and to God's covenant.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.desc: Archeological traces of Abraham's descendants; the events surrounding Dinah, daughter of Jacob; how their clan is forced to leave Canaan; the story of Joseph's bondage in Egypt; the plausibility of Joseph's rise to the grand vizier to the Pharaoh.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.desc: Parallels between the history of Ancient Egypt and the book of Exodus; evidence that the Hebrews in Egypt are forced into slave labor; how the biblical story of Moses correlates with earlier legends and Theban history; the event of the Burning Bush.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.desc: How the biblical story of the turning of the Nile to blood and the plagues of flies, locusts and hailstorms brought by God may be inspired by actual events; the exact route of the Exodus; historical perspectives on key features of the journey.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.sub-title: The Settlement in the Promised Land
programme.desc: How Joshua succeeds Moses as a military commander; the heroic saga of Joshua's conquests; the rise of the Philistines; their aggression against the Egyptians and the Canaanites; evidence that the Israelites settle in the highlands of Canaan.

programme.title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
programme.sub-title: The Rise of the Israelite Monarchy
programme.desc: The transformation of the Israelite tribes into the beginnings of a nation; how the tribes spread across Canaan; how they coalesce around a supreme commander, making Saul the first Israelite king; the rise of David as the successor to Saul.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: Professor Koester introduces one of the most discussed books of all time; the Book of Revelation, also known as the Apocalypse; the original meaning of apocalypse; the importance of the apocalyptic tradition; the three-part structure of the course.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The world of the Hebrew prophets, whose writings deeply influence the author of the Apocalypse; the themes of evil and hope in such works as Ezekiel and Isaiah; how these themes are taken up in the Dead Sea Scrolls and the apocalyptic book of Daniel.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The apocalyptic worldview, with its sense of conflicting powers, is transformed by Christian writers in the New Testament; apocalyptic themes have a primary place in the early church; the religious matrix out of which the book of Revelation arises.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.sub-title: Origins of the Book of Revelation
programme.desc: A close study of the text of the Apocalypse; looking behind the legends to surmise what can be said about its origins and author, identified only as John; examining the peculiar quality of John's Greek, which is not apparent in most translations.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The first two chapters of Revelation discuss the issues of the Christian communities that first receive the book; the experiences of the men and women addressed by John; the nature of the persecution and other problems; who this book is written for.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.sub-title: God, the Lamb, and the Seven Seals

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The middle section of the Apocalypse from two perspectives; the futurist view that Revelation is a book of ominous predictions; the literary view that seeks to understand how John organizes his details into a narrative that is surprisingly hopeful.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.desc: Studying images of the Arthurian legend and their relationship to historical reality; tracing the history of post-Roman Britain; the large-scale invasions of the Anglo-Saxons; evidence that a single individual rose up to lead his people.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.desc: Investigating archeological and historical evidence that supports the existence of an Arthur-like figure in early Britain; studying the site of Cadbury Castle, the center of operations of a leader who thwarted the Saxons; the supposed tomb of Arthur.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.sub-title: King Arthur in the Latin Chronicles
programme.desc: Exploring some of the most significant early witnesses to the Arthurian legend; studying accounts of Arthur's exploits and death in Latin texts and the Welsh Annales Cambriae; how texts from the 11th and 12th century C.E. embellished the legend.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.sub-title: King Arthur in Wales - The Mabinogion
programme.desc: How Arthur became a cultural touchstone in early Welsh history; key references to the Arthurian saga in the Black Book of Carmarthen and the Triads of the Island of Britain; the portrayal of Arthur in the tales of the Mabinogion.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.desc: The importance of Geoffrey of Monmouth's "The History of the Kings of Britain"; the political nature of the text; notable elements and characters; how Geoffrey established the basics of the Arthurian legend as they are currently known.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.sub-title: The Round Table - Arthur in Wace and Layamon
programme.desc: The contributions of the Anglo-Norman scribe Wace, who translated Geoffrey of Monmouth's text into Old Northern French; the English cleric Layamon, who created the first comprehensive account of Arthur in English; comparing Wace and Layamon's works.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.sub-title: Chrétien de Troyes and Sir Lancelot
programme.desc: Chretien de Troyes introducing elements of the Arthurian legend that would become essential; how de Troyes pioneered the genre of medieval romance, developed the ethos of courtly love and introduced the great heroic figure of Lancelot.

programme.title: King Arthur: History and Legend
programme.sub-title: Arthurian Tales in Brittany and Burgundy
programme.desc: Encountering the works of Marie de France, whose Arthurian writings developed themes of romantic love, the magical and the noble; how Robert de Boron linked King Arthur to the spiritual and religious realms; the introduction of the Holy Grail.
